bibnets: Importing, Constructing, and Exporting Bibliometric Networks

Source: R/bibnets-package.R
bibnets-package.Rd

bibnets builds bibliometric networks from the exports of scholarly databases. A bibliometric network links authors, documents, references, keywords, journals, institutions or countries through the records they share: co-authorship links authors who write together, co-citation links references cited together (Small, 1973), and bibliographic coupling links documents that cite the same work (Kessler, 1963). These networks show how a research field is organized: its collaborating groups, its intellectual base and its topics. The weight of a link can be normalized for how active each entity is (normalize()), and authorship credit can be counted in full, fractionally or by author position (the counting argument of the builders). Networks can be built for time windows (temporal_network()), reduced to their backbone with the disparity filter (backbone(); Serrano et al., 2009), and traced over time with a historiograph of the most locally cited documents (historiograph(); Garfield, 2004).

Records are read with read_biblio() from Scopus, Web of Science, OpenAlex, BibTeX, RIS, Lens.org, Dimensions and Crossref exports, or taken from any data frame with its own column names and separators. The builders (author_network(), document_network(), reference_network(), keyword_network(), source_network(), institution_network(), country_network() and the generic conetwork()) return an edge list with from, to, weight and count columns, which to_igraph(), to_tbl_graph(), to_cograph(), to_gephi(), to_graphml() and to_matrix() export.

References

Garfield, E. (2004). Historiographic mapping of knowledge domains literature. Journal of Information Science, 30(2), 119–145. doi:10.1177/0165551504042802

Kessler, M. M. (1963). Bibliographic coupling between scientific papers. American Documentation, 14(1), 10–25. doi:10.1002/asi.5090140103

Serrano, M. A., Boguna, M., & Vespignani, A. (2009). Extracting the multiscale backbone of complex weighted networks. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 106(16), 6483–6488.

Small, H. (1973). Co-citation in the scientific literature: A new measure of the relationship between two documents. Journal of the American Society for Information Science, 24(4), 265–269.
